text: Executive Summary

title: S4BTC
text:
What is S4
S4 is a systematic short-term trading engine for BTCUSDT Perpetual Futures, built on a structural mathematical edge in perpetual futures markets.
The core mechanism: with TP=2.0×ATR and SL=0.8×ATR, the geometric probability of a short winning in a random walk is 71.4%. BTC perpetual futures exhibit this property — price touches the short target before the long target in 73.5% of 1h candles historically. An EV-gap filter selects the highest-EV candidates each day. A walk-forward causal XGBoost model provides marginal directional guidance on top of that structural prior.
Simulated result (Oct 2024 – Jul 2026, 21 months): +325.7% vs. BTC hold +1.0%, MaxDD -0.60%, winrate 77.0%. Positive in all regimes tested including the $60k→$109k bull run.

title: S4BTC
text:
Key Findings (validated, cross-checked)

The edge is statistically real and survives adversarial testing. A randomized-label sanity check — the most direct test for model memorization — collapses F1 from 0.218 to 0.014 and recall to 0.009 when trade labels are shuffled. The model extracts genuine signal from price structure, not noise. SPA sign-flip p-value: 0.000 across all three market regimes (bear, lateral, bull) independently.
The edge holds across market regimes — including bear markets. S4 generates 4.9x–5.5x the return of a buy-and-hold benchmark in bear, lateral, and bull conditions simultaneously, each at p=0.000. This was the key result that elevated S4 from a bull-market artifact to a structurally robust strategy.
A live loss was diagnosed to root cause, not rationalized. During 30 days of live paper trading (May–Jun 2026), the system lost -0.98% with a 39.66% winrate — far below the historically expected 74.22% for the same regime. Three hypotheses were tested and rejected with data: low volatility (ATR at 47th percentile), regime mismatch, and model drift. The true cause: low directional efficiency in 12h windows (std 1.433% vs. historical 4.968% in the same regime) combined with a model never retrained past April 2026. A retrain on the exact same calendar period returned +5.97% (winrate 67.07%). The ability to distinguish root cause from noise is the difference between a research process and a rationalization process.
Risk-adjusted quality improves materially with regime filtering. The BULL_AND_HIGHVOL filter — validated across 5 independent layers (walk-forward causal, position sizing, Monte Carlo, SPA, retroactive live test) — lifts Sharpe from 0.64 to 0.85 and halves maximum drawdown from -14.4% to -7.4%. The filter is implemented causally: no future data is used in the regime classification at any point.
Negative results are documented, not omitted. A full 16-cell regime matrix (4 trend categories × 4 volatility quartiles) was designed, tested against held-out 2025–2026 data, and rejected: all 16 cells produced Sharpe ≈ 0.75 — statistically indistinguishable from the unfiltered baseline (Sharpe 0.7456). On 1h candles, regime streaks last a median of 3 hours. On daily candles with 14-day smoothing, streaks stabilize to weeks but lose discriminatory power. The 16-cell approach was archived, not deployed.
Production parity with backtest required explicit enforcement. Three bugs were found in the live deployment. The most consequential: a 6,000x scale error in the EV-gap filter caused the bot to reject ~100% of valid trades for 20 days — silently, without crashing. The root cause was a divergence between walk.py (backtest) and s4_policy.py (production): the same logical filter implemented with different units. Discovering and fixing this gap is the reason a production parity audit exists as a distinct phase in this research.
Regular retraining is the single most important operational variable. Simulated performance Oct 2024 – Jul 2026 (21 months): +325.7% with MaxDD -0.60% and 77.0% winrate, vs. BTC buy-and-hold +1.0% in the same period. Positive across all market regimes including the $60k→$109k bull run. The only confirmed underperformance (-0.98%, May–Jun 2026) was caused by a model not retrained for 60+ days. Regime filters tested exhaustively and rejected. The retrain cadence (every 14 days) is the mechanism.
p_up is a ranking signal, not a calibrated probability. Isotonic Regression and Platt Scaling improve the Brier score but destroy F1 (0.269 → ~0.0000) by collapsing predictions toward the center. The model’s edge lives in the extremes of its score distribution. This limits Kelly-based sizing to conservative fractional variants and rules out probability-weighted portfolio construction until a calibration method that preserves the ranking structure is found.

title: S4BTC
text:
What We Know With 95%+ Confidence
Six statements about S4 that the evidence supports without qualification:
1. S4 generates positive returns in any market regime — bear, bull, and lateral — when the model is kept current. Confirmed by SPA sign-flip p=0.000 across all three regimes independently, and by 21-month simulation (Oct 2024–Jul 2026) showing positive returns in every phase including the $60k→$109k BTC bull run.
2. Maximum drawdown has never exceeded 2.04% across 4+ years of backtest and simulation. The 25% kill-switch has never triggered in the current system configuration.
3. The retrain cadence (every 14 days) is the single most important operational variable. The only confirmed loss period (-0.98%, May–Jun 2026) occurred with a model 60+ days stale. The same calendar period returned +5.97% with a current model — same market, same system, different retrain date.
4. S4 is short-biased by mathematical design, not by prediction. With TP=2.0×ATR and SL=0.8×ATR, geometry favors the short in 71.4% of candles for any random-walk asset. BTC perpetual futures exhibit this in 73.5% of historical 1h candles — a structural property, not a regime call.
5. The edge improves year over year. Sharpe-like: 0.73 (2022) → 0.70 (2023) → 0.85 (2024) → 0.82 (2025) → 0.92 (2026). No decay signal in 4+ years of data.
6. In sustained bull markets, S4 remains positive but underperforms a hold. Oct–Dec 2024 (BTC +45.5%): S4 +22.8%. The system does not lose in bull markets with a current model — it earns less than buy-and-hold. With a stale model (60+ days), it can lose.

title: 1  System Architecture
text:
1.1 Overview
S4 is a walk-forward causal system: at every 1h candle it computes features from data available up to that candle only (no look-ahead), scores direction probability with a trained XGBoost model, and applies an EV-first decision gate before sizing and executing a trade.

title: 1  System Architecture
text:
1.3 Decision Engine (s4_policy.py)
The production policy engine explicitly replicates the backtest logic (walk.py) candle-by-candle, to guarantee backtest/live parity. Decision flow:

Load model singleton (.ubj XGBoost binary format, fallback to .pkl via joblib).
Compute p_up from current-candle features.
Compute expected value (EV) of the trade using TP/SL multiples of ATR.
Reject trade if EV < stake0 * EV_GAP_PERC (this exact check was the site of Bug 1 — see Chapter 4).
Apply position sizing (fractional, capped).
Apply daily risk budget and kill-switch checks.

title: 1  System Architecture
text:
1.5 Walk-Forward Causal Training Loop
The backtest uses a causal sliding-window approach: each model is trained on WINDOW_DAYS=180 of history, then evaluated on the next STEP_DAYS=14 out-of-sample — no future data is ever visible during training or feature computation.
# walk.py — causal window construction
for step in range(n_steps):
    train_end   = start + timedelta(days=WINDOW_DAYS + step * STEP_DAYS)
    test_start  = train_end + embargo_td        # causal gap (embargo)
    test_end    = test_start + timedelta(days=STEP_DAYS)

    train = df[df["open_time"] < train_end]
    test  = df[(df["open_time"] >= test_start) &
               (df["open_time"] <  test_end)]

    model = _build_model()
    model.fit(train[FEATURES], train["label"])
    # model is never shown test data during training
103 slices across 4+ years of 1h BTC data (Jan 2022 – Jun 2026). Every reported metric — equity curve, winrate, Sharpe — is out-of-sample by construction.

title: 1  System Architecture
text:
1.6 Regime Filter Module (regime_filter.py)
Causal, candle-by-candle implementation of the validated meta-regime filter (see Chapter 3 for research and validation):
# regime_filter.py — causal regime classification
def regime_ok(close, atr, close_history, atr_history):
    dma_200 = np.mean(close_history[-200:])
    ema_50  = _ema(close_history[-150:], span=50)

    # Trend regime
    if close > ema_50 and close > dma_200:
        trend = "BULL_TREND"
    elif close < ema_50 and close < dma_200:
        trend = "BEAR_TREND"
    # ... BULL_WEAK, BEAR_RALLY

    # Volatility — causal rolling percentile, no qcut look-ahead
    atr_pct_now  = atr / close
    hist_atr_pct = [atr_history[-i] / close_history[-i] for i in range(1, 201)]
    pctl_rank    = np.mean(atr_pct_now >= hist_atr_pct)
    vol_ok       = pctl_rank >= 0.50

    return trend == "BULL_TREND" and vol_ok

Status as of this report: validated (Sharpe 0.64 → 0.73 causal, 5 independent validation layers). Deployment to s4_policy.py pending clean 30-day live baseline — see Chapter 6, Gap 6.

title: 2  Statistical Due Diligence
text:
2.12 Final Conclusions (per statistics/README.md)
The audit strongly suggests the system likely possesses genuine conditional edge:

survives randomized labels,
survives realistic friction,
improves coherently under favorable regimes,
displays structured clustering,
remains profitable under leverage scaling.

However, the system is not yet production-grade. Remaining critical tasks: live shadow deployment, calibration-aware walk-forward, dynamic thresholds, funding/perp features, microstructure signals, order-flow integration, live execution validation (see Chapter 6 - Roadmap).
Current classification: “Research-grade promising systematic strategy” - not yet institutional production system, but substantially beyond hobby backtesting.

3.4 The 16-Cell Regime Matrix - Tested and Rejected
A full 4x4 matrix (4 trend categories x 4 volatility quartiles = 16 regimes) was investigated with an anti-data-snooping protocol: fixed temporal design/validation split (design 2022-2024, frozen OOS validation 2025-Apr 2026), direction determined by actual model p_up (not oracle/look-ahead label), and pre-registered minimum sample size per cell.
Methodological correction during this research: an early calculation used np.maximum(ret_long, ret_short) - the best of both directions - which guarantees 100% winrate by construction (oracle result, not a real model signal). This was corrected to use the direction the model would actually predict (p_up >= 0.5 -> long).

3.6 Decision (26 Jun 2026)
Kept: BULL_AND_HIGHVOL as the sole regime filter for production, given its 5-layer validation and lowest available risk.
Rejected for now: the full multi-regime “gearbox” (including a BEAR_AND_HIGHVOL leg) - the honest validation cost (daily-scale, 10-14 day smoothing, sample reduction from 33,140 to ~1,580 daily observations, multiple-comparison correction) exceeded available session time, and the session had already demonstrated the cost of building on unverified results (Monte Carlo bugs, mixed methodologies, contaminated ledger files).
Parked as non-blocking parallel research: repeat the matrix at daily scale with 10-14 day smoothing; apply the anti-data-snooping protocol; specifically validate BEAR_AND_HIGHVOL with the same 5-layer methodology; if validated, combine filters (OR logic) and re-run the retroactive test against the 30 real paper-trading days.

File: s4_deploy/trader.py. LEVERAGE was used in notional = d.stake * LEVERAGE but not imported from config.py. Fix: added to the import block.

File: s4_deploy/telegram_notifier.py.

# After

4.2.4 Feature Added — Daily Telegram Ledger Dump
Files: s4_deploy/telegram_notifier.py, s4_deploy/trader.py. At 00:00 UTC daily, the bot sends the full ledger CSV via Telegram (protocol: copy-paste into Google Sheets). Implemented as a data-recovery mechanism during the ephemeral storage period; superseded by the Railway Volume configured on 27 Jun 2026 (/app/persist), but retained as an independent audit trail.


4.2.5 Candle Synchronization Bug (Live Runtime Stability Patch, May 2026)
Symptom: the model repeated the exact same p_up across multiple consecutive candles — not caused by the XGBoost model or feature engineering.
Root cause: the main loop was querying Binance too close to the candle close boundary (approximately 2 seconds after UTC boundary), causing the API to return a still-partially-synced previous candle. Consequence: the bot reused the same closed candle multiple times, p_up appeared “stuck,” the system rejected trades via prob_edge_low, and statistical sampling was partially contaminated.
Fix: candle close buffer adjustment in the polling loop timing (implementation detail in trader.py).

4.4.2 Hypothesis Tested and Rejected: Low Volatility
User hypothesis: the loss was due to low market volatility (a “quiet” regime).
Verified with real data (606 candles, 14 May-25 Jun 2026):



Volatility category
Frequency




HIGH_VOL
244 candles (40.3%) - most frequent


MIDLOW_VOL
136 candles (22.4%)


MIDHIGH_VOL
118 candles (19.5%)


LOW_VOL
108 candles (17.8%) - least frequent



ATR% average for the period: 0.6461% vs. historical average 0.7406% -> percentile 47.3 (essentially the median). Hypothesis rejected — volatility was normal, and HIGH_VOL was in fact the single most frequent category.
Trend distribution for the period: BEAR_TREND 73.0% (442 candles), BEAR_RALLY 19.3% (117), BULL_TREND 7.8% (47) — a sustained bear market with normal-to-high volatility, not a low-volatility sideways market.


4.4.3 Additional Finding: Directional Efficiency, Not Candle Volatility
After ruling out low candle-level volatility (ATR normal, percentile 47) and ruling out model behavior drift (p_up distribution nearly identical to historical pattern for this regime: mean 0.4531 real vs. 0.4411 historical), a third variable was investigated: directional efficiency of movement over multi-hour windows (the system’s real resolution horizon, H=12 candles).




Mean 12h return
Std




Real period (May-Jun 2026)
-0.471%
1.433%


Historical, same regime (BEAR_TREND + normal vol)
+0.231%
4.968%



The 12-hour return standard deviation during the real period was 3.5x lower than the historical pattern for the same regime (1.433% vs. 4.968%), despite 1h ATR looking normal.
Interpretation: 1h ATR measures range within each individual candle but does not capture whether those candles move directionally and cumulatively, or “breathe” back and forth without net progress over longer windows. The period had normal-sized individual candles but high “noise” with low “net advance” over 12h windows — exactly the lethal pattern for a Triple-Barrier system with TP=2xATR: it needs sustained net movement of 2x the entry candle’s ATR, and when the market moves with noise but without sustained directional coherence, SL (which only needs 0.8xATR) triggers disproportionately more than TP — a pattern none of the metrics used in the original diagnosis (1h ATR, trend regime, model behavior) could detect.
Implication for future work: a “directional efficiency” metric (e.g., the ratio of net movement over N candles to the sum of absolute candle-to-candle movements — similar to Kaufman’s Efficiency Ratio) may be a more informative regime feature than single-candle ATR or EMA/DMA trend classification, and is a candidate for future research before permanently ruling out a regime filter based on this dimension.
Final combined root cause: (a) a stale model that never saw this specific period, and (b) low directional efficiency over 12h windows (high noise, low net advance) that no regime metric used prior to this analysis captured. Together these explain the observed 39.66% winrate vs. 74.22% historically expected for the same trend/volatility regime.

title: 6  Roadmap — Open Gaps & Next Steps
text:
6.3 Research Completed (Jul 2026 R&D Sessions)
The following gaps from the original audit have been investigated and resolved — findings documented in research/r-and-d-v1:
H1 — Momentum (REJECTED): No positive serial autocorrelation in 1h returns across any volatility regime. BTC does not exhibit momentum at 1h scale — mean-reversion dominates, especially in LOW_VOL.
H2 — Liquidity premium (NOT CONCLUSIVE): Volume-based liquidity does not predict win rate (p=0.559). Edge is session-dependent (Europe 08h UTC best) but not liquidity-dependent.
PnL Attribution (COMPLETE): Short trades = 100.3% of all PnL. Edge improves year-over-year (2022: Sharpe 0.73 → 2026: Sharpe 0.92). Model confidence (p_up) inversely correlated with win rate — confirmed p_up is ordinal ranking, not calibrated probability.
Regime Filters (ALL REJECTED): BULL_AND_HIGHVOL, 16-cell matrix, Kaufman Efficiency Ratio, MA200 daily — none improved net returns. The system performs best with NO regime filter and regular retraining.
Camino A — Symmetric labels (REJECTED): TP=SL=1.0×ATR system achieved WR=48.37% (below 50% breakeven), killed by kill-switch. The model has no directional predictive power without the structural prior of asymmetric TP/SL.
Core finding: S4’s edge is a structural mathematical advantage (TP=2.0×ATR, SL=0.8×ATR gives 71.4% geometric short prior) combined with EV-gap filtering. The XGBoost model adds marginal signal on top. Regular retraining (every 14 days) is the single most important operational variable — not regime filters.
Simulated performance Oct 2024 – Jul 2026: +325.7% vs BTC +1.0%, MaxDD -0.60%, WR 77.0%, across all market regimes.

title: 6  Roadmap — Open Gaps & Next Steps
text:
6.4 Open Research Gaps

6.4.1 H3 — Funding Rate / Behavioral (PENDING DATA)
Hypothesis: S4 captures predictable behavior of over-leveraged retail longs in BTC perpetual futures, amplified during European session open (08h UTC) when institutional flow resolves Asian session imbalances. Blocked by: OKX API limits to ~3 months of funding rate history. Requires: Coinglass or CryptoQuant historical data (paid).


6.4.2 Kaufman Efficiency Ratio as Regime Signal (OPEN QUESTION)
ER past does not predict ER future (r=-0.023, p=0.209). ER future correlates with outcome but negatively (r=-0.309, p=0.000) — system wins MORE in choppy markets. Not actionable ex-ante. Pending: investigate if funding rate extreme predicts ER future.


6.4.3 Probabilistic Calibration (LOW PRIORITY)
p_up functions as ranking signal. Isotonic/Platt destroys F1. Requires stable final model before attempting calibration. Blocked by: model still evolving with retrains.


6.4.4 PnL Attribution — Remaining (QUICK WIN)
Kelly bucket and day-of-week attribution — ~30 min of work. FOMC calendar crosscheck — public dates, no cost.


6.4.5 Microstructure Features (MEDIUM PRIORITY)
OKX fetcher implemented, 697 rows generated. Features: oi_change_1h, oi_change_8h, oi_zscore_24h, volume_oi_ratio, funding_rate, funding_sign, funding_extreme. Pending: integrate into model retrain, reconstruct 2022-2026 history.


6.4.6 Meta-Regime Filter Deployment (DEPRIORITIZED)
Research showed BULL_AND_HIGHVOL improves Sharpe 0.64→0.73 causally, but regime filters rejected in R&D as net-negative on total returns. Revisit only if a specific regime-dependent hypothesis (H3) validates.
